svg.title: Constraint-checked geometric layouts for padlocks and hairpins
svg.desc: Declared strand identity and pairing constraints feed topology-specific placement and flexible routing. FoldLayout checks pairing, collinearity and crossings. Actual synthetic padlock and hairpin drawings illustrate this schematic layout; it does not predict free energy or a preferred molecular conformation.

text.tspan: Sequence-resolved geometric layout of a declared topology
From molecular constraints to a drawing
Some complex topologies compare deterministic routes using length and bend costs.
The examples below use topology-specific routes, rather than a route search.
Two arm sites on one target; flexible backbone
Two declared stem spans; an unpaired loop
Declared pairing, strand identity and layout constraints
are checked for these supplied molecular objects.
Thermodynamic prediction is outside this model
No free-energy minimization or preferred-fold search;
a schematic fold does not establish reaction yield.
